slides.heading: Find Three Largest Numbers
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Easy · Searching
slides.narration: Let's solve Find Three Largest Numbers, an easy searching problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Return the three largest values (sorted ascending) without sorting the input.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Return the three largest values (sorted ascending) without sorting the input.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Keep a tiny sorted window of the three largest seen so far, and shift values into place as larger ones arrive.
slides.narration: Keep a tiny sorted window of the three largest seen so far, and shift values into place as larger ones arrive.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Sort the array and take the last three → O(n log n)
Optimal: one pass with three slots → O(n)
slides.narration: Sorting and taking the last three costs n log n. A single pass that maintains three slots does it in linear time with constant space.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Compare each number with the largest slot first
3. Shift smaller values down to make room
slides.narration: Step by step. First, start with three empty slots. Second, compare each number with the largest slot first. Third, shift smaller values down to make room. Fourth, return the three values ascending.

slides.narration: For each number we compare against the largest slot first, then the middle, then the smallest, and a small shift-and-insert helper moves the smaller values down.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Negative numbers: start slots as empty, not 0
Shift order matters: move down before overwriting
slides.narration: Initialise slots as empty rather than zero, or negatives break. Duplicates may occupy multiple slots, and shifting must happen before you overwrite.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: k largest → min-heap of size k, O(n log k)
slides.narration: For k largest, use a min-heap of size k, or quickselect.
